paragraphs.text: Hello everyone. My name is Lê Đỗ Thanh Ngân. I am in Class 3A7. Today, I would like to tell you about my hero, Alexander Fleming, and how his story inspires my dream.
Alexander Fleming was a Scottish doctor and scientist.
In 1928, he noticed something unusual in his laboratory.
A kind of mould had grown on a dish, and the bacteria around it had disappeared.
Instead of ignoring it, he became curious and studied it carefully.
This discovery led to penicillin, an important medicine that helps doctors treat many bacterial infections.
In 1945, Fleming shared the Nobel Prize for this discovery and its development.
I admire Alexander Fleming for three reasons.
First, he was curious. He asked questions and looked carefully at things other people might miss.
Second, he was patient and determined. Discoveries do not always happen quickly, and scientists need to keep learning.
Third, his work helped people around the world. He did not just learn something new; his discovery became important for human health.
His story teaches me that a small observation can lead to a big change.
We do not have to be famous or grown-up to make a difference.
We can start by noticing a problem and doing something helpful.
My dream is to help make my school a healthier and kinder place.
I want to start a "Healthy Heroes" project with my classmates.
We could make simple posters about washing our hands, eating healthy food, and keeping our classrooms clean.
We could also remind one another to ask a trusted adult or a doctor before taking medicine.
Medicine can help us, but we must use it safely.
I know I cannot discover a new medicine today.
But I can be curious, learn more about science, and take small actions to help others.
If my project helps even one friend build a healthy habit, I will be happy.
And if we work together, we may help many more people.
Alexander Fleming used his curiosity to help the world.
I want to use my curiosity, kindness, and knowledge to do the same in my own small way.
Great changes can begin with small actions.
I may be young, but I can start today!
Thank you for listening!
